target.title: fix(feishu): cap sender-name and streaming token caches
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two unbounded in-process Maps in the Feishu plugin:

1. **`senderNameCache`** — sender display name lookups with no eviction under high message volume.
2. **`tokenCache`** — streaming-card tenant access token cache with no eviction.

## Why This Change Was Made

Applies `pruneMapToMaxSize` after each cache write: sender names capped at **500**, streaming tokens at **256**, both with LRU eviction.

## User Impact

Long-lived Feishu gateways get bounded memory for sender-name and streaming-token caches. Normal workloads below the caps are unchanged.

## Evidence

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  extensions/feishu/src/bot-sender-name.test.ts \
  extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Feishu sender-name and streaming token caches grew without bound.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS (Darwin arm64), Node.js v22.22.0, local source checkout on branch `fix/feishu-cap-sender-and-token-caches`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/feishu/src/bot-sender-name.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
 ✓ evicts oldest sender name cache entries once the cache exceeds its cap
 ✓ evicts oldest streaming token cache entries once the cache exceeds its cap

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  25 passed (25)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Regression tests exercise production cache helpers and confirm oldest entries are evicted at cap while newest entries remain cached.
- **What was not tested:** Live Feishu/Lark API token fetch or contact lookup.
